content: The nose is an anatomical structure in vertebrates that protrudes from the face and contains the nostrils, also known as nares. These nostrils allow air to enter and exit the body for respiration, working in conjunction with the mouth. In most humans, the nose also contains nasal hairs, which serve to trap airborne particles and prevent them from reaching the lungs. Inside and behind the nose, there are specialized structures such as the olfactory mucosa and the sinuses. Air that passes through the nasal cavity subsequently moves into the pharynx, a shared pathway with the digestive system, before continuing into the rest of the respiratory system. In humans, the nose is centrally located on the face, whereas in most other mammals, it is positioned at the upper tip of the snout. The nose serves as an interface between the body and the external environment, performing additional functions such as conditioning the air that enters. This includes warming and humidifying the air, as well as reclaiming moisture from exhaled air, a process that is particularly efficient in animals like camels. In most mammals, the nose is the primary organ for the sense of smell. When an animal sniffs, air flows through the nose and over structures in the nasal cavity called turbinates. These turbinates create turbulence, slowing the airflow and directing it toward the olfactory epithelium. At the surface of the olfactory epithelium, odor molecules in the air interact with olfactory receptor neurons. These neurons transduce the molecular features of the odors into non-painful electrical signals that are processed by the brain. In cetaceans, such as whales and dolphins, the nose has evolved into a reduced form consisting only of the nostrils, which have migrated to the top of the head. This adaptation allows for a more streamlined body shape and enables these animals to breathe while remaining mostly submerged in water. In contrast, the elephant's nose has developed into a highly specialized, elongated, muscular organ known as the trunk, which is capable of complex manipulation.
